faqs.q: Sec. 26-43. - Duties of the community resilience coordinator.
faqs.a:
The community resilience coordinator shall:
(a)
Comply with all requirements issued by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)
                  and the Colorado Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management Agency (DHSEM)
                  in order to procure the maximum amount of federal and state assistance and grant monies
                  for the city.
(b)
Ensure that the local emergency operations plan (EOP) is kept current.
(c)
Act as liaison with all local emergency response agencies and ensure their cooperation
                  in drafting their portions of the plan. All departments over which the city has authority
                  shall provide such cooperation in planning.
(d)
Develop, coordinate, and conduct a schedule of training to ensure that all persons
                  with specific responsibilities under the EOP understand their duties and are capable
                  of performing their duties in accordance with DHSEM and FEMA. All persons with specific
                  responsibilities under the EOP shall comply with, and participate in, the training
                  schedule to understand their duties and be capable of performing their duties. The
                  EOP shall be tested as deemed necessary by the community resilience coordinator or
                  the city manager.
(e)
Prepare and coordinate exercises of the EOP as mandated by DHSEM and FEMA.
(f)
Conduct debriefings in the aftermath of EOP exercises and revise the EOP to reflect
                  lessons learned.
(g)
Assist the city manager in negotiating and entering into mutual aid agreements.
(h)
Coordinate resources for the city manager or their designee and perform all other
                  duties assigned by the city manager or their designee in the response to a civil emergency,
                  emergency, or disaster.
(i)
Cooperate and coordinate with state and federal authorities in the aftermath of a
                  civil emergency, emergency or disaster to ensure the maximum available support for
                  recovery and assistance for persons and businesses.
(j)
Develop or implement a mitigation plan for the city in cooperation with all city departments
                  and agencies. All agencies over which the city has authority shall provide cooperation
                  in mitigation planning.
(k)
Work through the city manager or their designee to ensure that requirements for infrastructure
                  replacement are consistent with current best practices to ensure the maximum assistance
                  from the federal government in the event that public facilities must be reconstructed
                  or replaced in the aftermath of a civil emergency, emergency, or disaster.
(
Ord. No. 4827
, § 2, 12-5-2022)
